page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor operating at 3.2 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It includes a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512F, AVX-512_VNNI, AVX-512_BF16, and AES cryptography. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the average tier for most compute tasks. It achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 8310.78 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4720.0. However, memory-bound operations reveal notable performance tradeoffs. While cached small-block memory reads reach 464.83 GB/sec, large-block uncached memory reads drop to a weak 37.74 GB/sec, which is reflected in a lower PassMark memory score of 1525.1. Database operations and physics simulations also fall into the bottom 25% of benchmarks. Furthermore, while small LLM inference is handled adequately, medium 7B LLM inference is poor, yielding only 5.16 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c4.2xlarge offers a dedicated compute profile with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it a resource-dense option for compute-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. It is well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, and lightweight text or image processing. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, large-scale physics simulations, or complex machine learning inference due to the identified memory bandwidth bottlenecks and lack of GPU acceleration.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated Intel Xeon 8369HB physical cores running at 3.2 GHz and 16.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, it includes a 33 MB L3 cache and supports AVX-512 and AES instruction sets. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data shows average performance in multi-core compute tasks, such as software compilation and static web serving, but reveals limitations in memory-intensive workloads. Uncached large-block memory reads and database operations perform in the bottom 25%, and medium LLM inference is poor. Consequently, this instance is best suited for dedicated, compute-heavy tasks like web serving and light image processing, rather than memory-heavy databases or advanced machine learning workloads.
